cards.title: Stop Building Generic AI: Builders Are Desperate for Reliable, Niche AI Tools That Actually Work
cards.thesis: While cutting-edge AI models like Claude Opus 5 continue to drop, builders are getting fed up with 'fragile and half-baked' AI tools from big tech, citing critical reliability issues like OpenAI's Codex (the AI behind code assistants) going down. This frustration creates a huge opening for focused, dependable AI assistants that solve specific, painful problems for builders, without the hype or instability.

evidence.text: Claude Opus 5 was just released, showing continued rapid advancement in AI models.

Big tech companies like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Meta are pushing for less regulation on 'open-weight models' (AI models whose inner workings are publicly available), indicating a desire for more flexibility and control outside of closed systems.
A Hacker News thread asks, 'Why does everything Microsoft create lately feel fragile and half-baked?' specifically mentioning they are 'rushing to force-feed us unfinished AI and web apps.'
OpenAI's foundational AI model, Codex, which powers many AI coding assistants, was reported as 'down' and 'being investigated.'
One user even asked, 'Can we get a day that is free from AI news?' suggesting fatigue with constant announcements and a desire for practical, stable solutions.

cards.opportunity: Everyone's swamped with AI hype, but builders are quietly fuming about unreliable, generic AI tools from big companies that often break or give bad info. Pick a super specific, annoying developer problem — like keeping API documentation for a niche framework automatically updated, or reliably generating test cases for a specific language — and build an AI tool that *just works* for that one thing. You could probably ship a prototype this weekend, and own a frustrated but eager market by focusing on bulletproof reliability over broad features.
